title: EIP-7918: Blob Base Fee Bounded by Execution Cost

sub_graphs.name: Reserve Price Parameter Definition
sub_graphs.description: Defines the BLOB_BASE_COST constant that establishes the minimum ratio between blob fees and execution fees. This constant sets the reserve price floor such that a blob must cost at least BLOB_BASE_COST execution gas worth of blob fees, enforcing a ratio of BLOB_BASE_COST / GAS_PER_BLOB (= 1/16) between the reserve blob base fee and the execution base fee.

invariants.text: The blob base fee will settle at a level where a blob costs at least BLOB_BASE_COST execution gas.
The ratio between the reserve price for the blob base fee and the execution base fee is fixed to BLOB_BASE_COST / GAS_PER_BLOB = 2**13 / 2**17 = 1/16.
The blob fee's share of the total price will always be at least BLOB_BASE_COST / (BLOB_BASE_COST + execution_cost) when the reserve price is active.

constants.name: BLOB_BASE_COST
constants.description: The minimum cost in execution gas units that a blob must effectively cost. Sets the reserve price floor for blob base fees relative to execution costs.

dependencies.description: Introduces blob transactions, GAS_PER_BLOB (2**17 = 131072), and the original calc_excess_blob_gas() function that this EIP modifies.
Introduces the blobSchedule configuration for referencing target and max blob counts, as well as baseFeeUpdateFraction.

sub_graphs.name: Excess Blob Gas Calculation (Modified)
sub_graphs.description: The core specification change: modifies calc_excess_blob_gas() from EIP-4844 to introduce a reserve price mechanism. When the reserve price (BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee_per_gas) exceeds the current blob cost (GAS_PER_BLOB * base_fee_per_blob_gas), the function enters the execution-fee-led pricing regime and does not subtract target_blob_gas, causing excess_blob_gas to increase monotonically according to blob_gas_used while capping the per-block maximum increase.

invariants.text: The per-block maximum increase in excess_blob_gas is unchanged from the original mechanism. In the reserve-price regime, the increase is bounded by blob_gas_used * (max - target) / max.
When total blob gas usage (excess + used) is below target, excess_blob_gas resets to 0 regardless of reserve price conditions.

functions.name: calc_excess_blob_gas

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: The parent block header containing excess_blob_gas, blob_gas_used, and base_fee_per_gas fields.

functions.description: Calculates the excess blob gas for the current block based on the parent block's state. Introduces a reserve price check that determines whether to operate in blob-fee-led or execution-fee-led pricing regime.

body_structure.label: reserve price check (execution-fee-led vs blob-fee-led regime)

external_calls.name: get_base_fee_per_blob_gas
external_calls.description: Computes the blob base fee from the parent header using fake_exponential() with the current blobSchedule.baseFeeUpdateFraction.

state_variables.name: excess_blob_gas
state_variables.description: Tracks the cumulative excess blob gas across blocks. Used as input to fake_exponential() to determine base_fee_per_blob_gas. Modified by this function each block.

state_variables.name: blob_gas_used
state_variables.description: The total blob gas consumed in a block. Equal to the number of blobs times GAS_PER_BLOB.

state_variables.name: base_fee_per_gas
state_variables.description: The execution layer base fee per gas for the block. Used in the reserve price comparison.

preconditions.text: The parent header must contain valid excess_blob_gas, blob_gas_used, and base_fee_per_gas fields.
The current block's blobSchedule must be used during processing, including the new baseFeeUpdateFraction, max, and target values after a fork.

postconditions.text: If under target: excess_blob_gas is exactly 0.
In execution-fee-led regime: excess_blob_gas increases without allowing any decrease (no target subtraction).
postconditions.formal: if reserve_price_active then result == parent.excess_blob_gas + parent.blob_gas_used * (blobSchedule.max - blobSchedule.target) // blobSchedule.max

postconditions.text: In blob-fee-led regime: excess_blob_gas follows the original EIP-4844 update rule.
postconditions.formal: if NOT reserve_price_active then result == parent.excess_blob_gas + parent.blob_gas_used - target_blob_gas

state_transitions.name: Under-Target Reset
state_transitions.description: When total blob gas (excess + used) is below target, excess resets to 0, effectively resetting the blob fee to its minimum.

state_transitions.name: Execution-Fee-Led Pricing Regime
state_transitions.description: When the reserve price exceeds the current blob cost, the function enters execution-fee-led mode. It increases excess_blob_gas proportionally to blob_gas_used without subtracting target_blob_gas, causing the blob fee to rise toward the reserve price floor.
state_transitions.from_state: excess_blob_gas where blob fee < reserve price

state_transitions.name: Blob-Fee-Led Pricing Regime (Original EIP-4844)
state_transitions.description: When the blob fee is at or above the reserve price, the standard EIP-4844 excess blob gas update rule applies, allowing both increases and decreases based on whether usage exceeds or falls below target.
state_transitions.from_state: excess_blob_gas where blob fee >= reserve price

dependencies.description: The amount of blob gas consumed per blob.
The target number of blobs per block, used to compute target_blob_gas.
The maximum number of blobs per block, used in the execution-fee-led update formula.
Used by fake_exponential() inside get_base_fee_per_blob_gas(). The new value must be used immediately after a fork.
Computes the blob base fee from the parent header using fake_exponential(). Must use the current blobSchedule.baseFeeUpdateFraction.

sub_graphs.name: Fee-Inelasticity and Reserve Price Economics
sub_graphs.description: Describes the economic rationale for the reserve price mechanism. When execution costs dominate blob costs, the demand curve for blobspace becomes inelastic (vertical), and the blob base fee mechanism loses its ability to control equilibrium quantity. The reserve price prevents the blob base fee from falling to 1 wei and restores the price signal function of the mechanism.

invariants.text: The reserve blob base fee is BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee_per_gas / GAS_PER_BLOB, maintaining a fixed ratio to execution costs.
The blob fee's share of total price (blob_fee + execution_cost) is always at least BLOB_BASE_COST / (BLOB_BASE_COST + execution_cost) when the reserve is active.

economic_properties.name: Demand Inelasticity Horizon
economic_properties.description: When execution costs c > 0, the demand curve Q(b + c) has an inelasticity horizon: as b -> 0, Q(b + c) -> Q(c). The demand curve becomes vertical and changes in b no longer affect demand Q.
economic_properties.formal: lim(b -> 0) Q(b + c) = Q(c) where c = execution_cost * base_fee_per_gas / GAS_PER_BLOB

economic_properties.name: Price Signal Restoration
economic_properties.description: The reserve price ensures the blob base fee remains a significant fraction of the total cost, allowing the fee update mechanism to converge on equilibrium in a timely manner rather than spiraling to 1 wei.

economic_properties.name: Equilibrium Formation
economic_properties.description: The equilibrium must form on the edge of the upper-left quadrant, at the intersection between the target supply curve and demand, or along the reserve price curve. The protocol avoids first-price auction fallback which is considered worse UX.

sub_graphs.name: KZG Proof Verification Cost Justification
sub_graphs.description: Provides the computational justification for requiring blob consumers to pay a minimum fee that reflects the compute cost imposed on nodes. KZG proof verification for blobs is computationally expensive, and the reserve price ensures consumers pay at least a relevant fraction of the market rate for node compute.

invariants.text: BLOB_BASE_COST is set relatively moderately compared to the actual compute costs that blobs impose on nodes (KZG proof verification costs approximately 15x a single point evaluation).

compute_cost_analysis.description: EL nodes batch-verify CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (128) cell proofs per blob before including a tx in their tx pool. This is roughly 15x more expensive than a single POINT_EVALUATION_PRECOMPILE_GAS operation.
Full nodes verify 4 custodied columns, each containing one cell from all blobs in the payload. Column cell proofs can be batch-verified.
Supernodes verify 128 custodied columns, each containing one cell from all blobs in the payload.
Nodes peer-sample SAMPLES_PER_SLOT (8) columns each slot in addition to custodied columns.

dependencies.description: Gas charged for a single point evaluation KZG proof verification via the precompile.
Number of cell proofs that must be verified per blob in PeerDAS.

sub_graphs.name: Fork Transition Handling
sub_graphs.description: Specifies the critical requirement that during the first block after a fork, the new blobSchedule parameters must be used immediately. This includes using the new baseFeeUpdateFraction in fake_exponential() when computing base_fee_per_blob_gas, and the new max and target values in calc_excess_blob_gas().

invariants.text: In the first block after a fork, fake_exponential() must use the new blobSchedule.baseFeeUpdateFraction when calculating base_fee_per_blob_gas via get_base_fee_per_blob_gas(parent).
In the first block after a fork, the new blobSchedule.max and blobSchedule.target must be used in calc_excess_blob_gas().

preconditions.text: The current block's blobSchedule must be resolved before calling calc_excess_blob_gas() or get_base_fee_per_blob_gas().

state_transitions.name: Fork Transition
state_transitions.description: On the first block of a new fork, all blobSchedule parameters (target, max, baseFeeUpdateFraction) switch to the new fork's values. This is a discrete transition that affects both the reserve price comparison and the excess blob gas computation.
state_transitions.trigger: Block is first block of new fork

sub_graphs.name: Delayed Response and Fee Convergence
sub_graphs.description: Describes the behavior during the execution-fee-led pricing regime where the blob base fee rises smoothly toward the reserve price without allowing decreases. When the execution base fee rises quickly, there may be a few blocks of lag before the blob base fee catches up, during which target_blob_gas is never subtracted.

invariants.text: In the execution-fee-led regime, the blob base fee can only increase, never decrease, since target_blob_gas is not subtracted.
invariants.formal: if reserve_price_active then excess_blob_gas(n+1) >= excess_blob_gas(n) for any non-zero blob_gas_used

invariants.text: The maximum per-block increase in excess_blob_gas is preserved regardless of pricing regime, ensuring no sudden fee spikes.

behavioral_properties.name: Monotonic Fee Increase in Reserve Regime
behavioral_properties.description: When in the execution-fee-led regime, the blob base fee increases monotonically with each block that contains blobs, providing smooth convergence toward the reserve price.

behavioral_properties.name: Bounded Convergence Lag
behavioral_properties.description: If the execution base fee rises quickly, there may be a temporary lag of a few blocks before the blob base fee catches up. During this period, the blob fee increases without any possibility of decrease.

behavioral_properties.name: Spike Prevention
behavioral_properties.description: Unlike the current mechanism where the blob base fee can fall to 1 wei and then require over an hour of near-full blocks to restore equilibrium, the reserve price prevents such dramatic drops and the resulting spiky resource consumption.

sub_graphs.name: Future Scalability Design
sub_graphs.description: Addresses the long-term sustainability of the reserve price as Ethereum scales. Because the reserve price is defined relative to the execution base fee rather than as a fixed absolute value, it naturally adjusts as both blobspace and blockspace scale. However, if blob throughput scales significantly faster than execution throughput, the reserve price could become relatively too high.

invariants.text: If Ethereum scales blockspace and blobspace roughly in synchrony, the reserve price remains at the desired level without requiring parameter changes.
invariants.formal: if scale(blobspace) ~ scale(blockspace) then BLOB_BASE_COST remains appropriate

scalability_analysis.name: Revenue Share Bound
scalability_analysis.description: At 1000 blobs and 30M execution gas per block, Ethereum would derive approximately 21.5% of income from blob gas even at the reserve price, suggesting BLOB_BASE_COST would be too high at that scale.

scalability_analysis.name: No Fixed Threshold Needed
scalability_analysis.description: Because the reserve price is proportional to the execution base fee rather than a fixed wei amount, it automatically adjusts with technological progress (Moore's law, Nielsen's law) without requiring governance intervention.

security_considerations.text: The blob base fee will settle at a level where a blob costs at least BLOB_BASE_COST execution gas. To the best of the authors' knowledge, there are no security risks associated with this.
security_considerations.mitigation: The mechanism is a simple if-clause addition to an existing function with well-understood behavior.

cross_references.description: EIP-7918 modifies the calc_excess_blob_gas() function originally defined in EIP-4844 by adding a reserve price check.
EIP-7918 uses the blobSchedule (target, max, baseFeeUpdateFraction) introduced in EIP-7840.
EIP-7918 references EIP-7594 (PeerDAS) for KZG proof verification cost analysis context.

title: EIP-7934: RLP Execution Block Size Limit

sub_graphs.name: Block Size Constants Definition
sub_graphs.description: Defines the protocol-level constants that govern the maximum allowed RLP-encoded execution block size. MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (10 MiB) is the absolute upper bound aligned with the CL gossip protocol limit. SAFETY_MARGIN (2 MiB) reserves space for beacon block overhead. MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE is the effective limit applied to RLP-encoded execution blocks, computed as MAX_BLOCK_SIZE - SAFETY_MARGIN.

invariants.text: MAX_BLOCK_SIZE must equal 10,485,760 bytes (10 MiB).
SAFETY_MARGIN must equal 2,097,152 bytes (2 MiB).
MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE must equal MAX_BLOCK_SIZE minus SAFETY_MARGIN, i.e. 8,388,608 bytes (8 MiB).
The relationship between the three constants is fixed and deterministic: MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE is always derived from the other two.

constants.name: MAX_BLOCK_SIZE
constants.description: The absolute maximum block size in bytes (10 MiB), aligned with the consensus layer gossip protocol propagation limit.

constants.name: SAFETY_MARGIN
constants.description: A 2 MiB margin reserved to accommodate beacon block wrapping overhead so that the total beacon block stays within the CL gossip limit.

constants.name: MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE
constants.description: The effective maximum RLP-encoded execution block size (8 MiB). Any execution block whose RLP encoding exceeds this value is invalid.

sub_graphs.name: Block Size Validation Function
sub_graphs.description: Defines the validation function exceed_max_rlp_block_size() that determines whether a given block exceeds the maximum allowed RLP-encoded size. This function is the core enforcement mechanism for the block size limit. It RLP-encodes the block, measures the byte length, and compares against MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE. A true return value means the block is invalid.

invariants.text: For any valid block B: the RLP-encoded size must not exceed MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE.
The block size check applies independently of gas-related metrics; gas limits and block size limits are orthogonal constraints.
invariants.formal: block_size_validity is independent of gas_used, gas_limit

functions.name: exceed_max_rlp_block_size

parameters.name: block
parameters.description: The execution block to be validated.

functions.return_description: Returns true if the block's RLP-encoded size exceeds MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (i.e. the block is invalid), false otherwise.
functions.source_code:
def exceed_max_rlp_block_size(block: Block) -> bool:
    return len(rlp.encode(block)) > MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE
functions.description: Encodes the block via RLP, measures the resulting byte length, and compares it against MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE. A true return value means the block is invalid and must be rejected or must not be built.

external_calls.name: rlp.encode
external_calls.description: RLP-encodes the full block into a byte sequence.

external_calls.name: len
external_calls.description: Returns the byte length of the RLP-encoded block.

preconditions.text: The block must be a fully constructed Block object capable of being RLP-encoded.
preconditions.formal: block is a valid Block instance with all fields populated

postconditions.text: If exceed_max_rlp_block_size returns true, the block MUST be treated as invalid: it must be rejected during validation and must not be propagated.
postconditions.formal: if exceed_max_rlp_block_size(block) == true then block.is_valid == false

postconditions.text: If exceed_max_rlp_block_size returns false, the block passes the size validity check (other validity checks still apply independently).
postconditions.formal: if exceed_max_rlp_block_size(block) == false then block passes size check

sub_graphs.name: Block Creation Constraint
sub_graphs.description: Validators and block builders must ensure the total RLP-encoded size of any produced block does not exceed MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE. This is a construction-time constraint that prevents oversized blocks from being proposed in the first place. Block assembly must monitor cumulative RLP size and stop including transactions before the limit is breached.

invariants.text: A validator MUST NOT propose a block whose RLP-encoded size exceeds MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE.
invariants.formal: for all proposed blocks B: len(rlp.encode(B)) <= MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE

preconditions.text: The block builder must have access to the RLP encoding function and must be able to measure or estimate the encoded size during block assembly.

postconditions.text: Every block produced by a compliant validator satisfies the size limit.

state_transitions.name: Block Assembly Size Check
state_transitions.description: During block assembly, if adding the next transaction would cause the block's RLP-encoded size to exceed MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE, the transaction must not be included and the block should be sealed at the current state.
state_transitions.trigger: Estimated RLP size after adding next transaction > MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE
state_transitions.from_state: Block under construction with current transactions
state_transitions.to_state: Block sealed without the oversizing transaction

references: EIP-7934 Specification: Changes to Protocol Behavior (Block Creation)

sub_graphs.name: Block Validation and Propagation Rules
sub_graphs.description: Nodes must reject blocks whose RLP-encoded size exceeds MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE during validation. All Ethereum client implementations must integrate this size check as part of their block validation and propagation pipeline. This check is independent of gas-based validation and must be applied to all received blocks.

invariants.text: A node MUST reject any received block whose RLP-encoded size exceeds MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE.
invariants.formal: for all received blocks B: if len(rlp.encode(B)) > MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE then reject(B)

invariants.text: A node MUST NOT propagate any block whose RLP-encoded size exceeds MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE.
invariants.formal: for all blocks B: if len(rlp.encode(B)) > MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE then do_not_propagate(B)

invariants.text: The block size validation is independent of gas-related metrics and must be enforced as a separate check.
invariants.formal: size_validation(B) is evaluated independently of gas_validation(B)

preconditions.text: A block has been received by the node via the network (p2p gossip or direct request).

postconditions.text: If the block's RLP-encoded size exceeds MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE, the block is marked invalid, is not stored in the canonical chain, and is not forwarded to peers.
postconditions.formal: if len(rlp.encode(B)) > MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE then B not in canonical_chain AND B not in gossip_output

postconditions.text: If the block's RLP-encoded size is within MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE, the block passes this validation step and proceeds to other validation checks.

state_transitions.name: Block Reception Validation
state_transitions.description: On receiving a new block: (1) compute len(rlp.encode(block)); (2) if > MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE, reject block and do not propagate; (3) if <= MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE, continue with remaining block validation steps.
state_transitions.to_state: Block rejected (if oversized) OR Block passes size check (if within limit)

references: EIP-7934 Specification: Changes to Protocol Behavior (Block Validation)

sub_graphs.name: Consensus Layer Compatibility and Network Safety
sub_graphs.description: The 10 MiB total cap (including the 2 MiB safety margin for beacon block overhead) ensures that execution blocks, when wrapped in beacon blocks, remain within the CL gossip protocol's propagation limit. Without this constraint, oversized blocks could fail to propagate at the CL level, causing network fragmentation or denial-of-service. The EIP provides inherent protection against deliberate oversized-block attacks.

invariants.text: The sum of the RLP-encoded execution block size and beacon block overhead must not exceed the CL gossip protocol's maximum message size (approximately 10 MiB).
MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8 MiB) + SAFETY_MARGIN (2 MiB) = MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (10 MiB), which aligns with the CL gossip propagation limit.

security_considerations.text: Blocks exceeding 10 MiB are not propagated by the CL gossip protocol, which could cause network fragmentation or denial-of-service conditions if the EL does not enforce its own limit.
security_considerations.mitigation: EIP-7934 introduces a protocol-level EL block size cap that prevents execution blocks from exceeding the CL propagation limit.

security_considerations.text: Without a protocol-level block size cap, malicious actors could generate exceptionally large blocks to disrupt network performance via slow propagation and increased risk of temporary forks and reorgs.
security_considerations.mitigation: The MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE limit makes it impossible to produce or accept blocks large enough to cause these issues.

security_considerations.text: Restricting maximum block size provides inherent protection against deliberate oversized-block attacks that target block validation times.
security_considerations.mitigation: The fixed 8 MiB RLP block size limit bounds the worst-case block validation and propagation time.

sub_graphs.name: Backwards Compatibility and Activation
sub_graphs.description: This EIP is not backward-compatible with any blocks larger than the newly specified size limit. Validators and miners must update their block construction logic to strictly respect this limit. All Ethereum client implementations must integrate the block size check before the EIP activation fork. After activation, all new blocks must satisfy the MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE constraint.

invariants.text: After activation, no block with RLP-encoded size exceeding MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE can be valid, regardless of when it was constructed.
invariants.formal: for all blocks B after activation: len(rlp.encode(B)) <= MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE

preconditions.text: All Ethereum client implementations must be updated to integrate the block size check before the EIP activation block/fork.

postconditions.text: Post-activation, all block construction, validation, and propagation paths enforce the MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE constraint.
postconditions.formal: post_activation: construction_enforces(MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE) AND validation_enforces(MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE) AND propagation_enforces(MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE)

state_transitions.name: Fork Activation Transition
state_transitions.description: At the activation fork boundary, the block size validation rule becomes active. From this point forward, all new blocks must satisfy len(rlp.encode(block)) <= MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE.
state_transitions.from_state: No protocol-level block size limit enforced
state_transitions.to_state: MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE constraint enforced on all block construction, validation, and propagation
